evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: The requested capability is clear and has a single reasonable interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: The action and object are specific enough to avoid materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website for info and updates
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “from the website” entails (UI form vs. automated mailing), and what qualifies as “all the trainers” (role, current year, training owners).

evaluations.evidence: a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: “Very clear map” is subjective and can be interpreted as different map types/levels of detail (campus map vs. floor plans vs. interactive directions).

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself ... and links to slides
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous scope of “edit” (which fields/sections) and unclear phrase “and links to slides” (add links? edit links? required?).

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “per day” means (calendar day vs. event day) and what constitutes a “registration” (training vs. summit vs. camp registration).

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status ... if attendend, refunded, no show
evaluations.rationale: Unclear set of statuses and definitions (e.g., “attended” vs. “no show”), and “helps track” can imply multiple different features (filters, dashboards, exports).

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous behavior of the waitlist (automatic promotion, ordering, notifications, per-session vs. per-day).

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “cancellation terms” are (which text/version) and where/when the checkbox is presented (registration, cancellation, both).

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: “Whatever workflow exists” is undefined and allows materially different implementations; “tie in” is also vague about enforcement vs. messaging.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Conditional phrasing makes the requirement unclear; “my schedule” and the underlying schedule feature are not defined.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: The requested information is specific and has a single reasonable interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: a view ... that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: “All attendee information” is undefined and could mean different data sets (PII, contact info, registration details, etc.).

evaluations.evidence: all trainee information is shown
evaluations.rationale: “All trainee information” is ambiguous and can be interpreted as different fields and privacy scopes.

evaluations.evidence: possibly a map view
evaluations.rationale: “Possibly” makes the requirement unclear (optional vs. conditional), leading to materially different interpretations of what must be delivered.

evaluations.evidence: clearly marked for the following information: day and time ... title ... short summary ...
evaluations.rationale: Despite the phrase “clearly marked,” the story enumerates the required fields and links, limiting interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: promote call for trainings
evaluations.rationale: “Promote” is vague and could mean a banner, CTA section, link, or marketing content with different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: have a link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: The requested link and destination are clear enough for a single interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Location and opening hours are concrete information needs with little room for divergent interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding Stripe-processed sponsorship payments is a clear capability, even if details are not specified.

evaluations.evidence: become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “$350 level sponsor” entails (benefits/role assignment) and what “become a sponsor role” means in the system.

evaluations.evidence: attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: “Associated with this company” is unclear (employer field, sponsorship purchaser, email domain, manually linked).

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “identify myself as” means (company name selection, verification, linking attendees) and what constitutes the sponsorship object.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Creating and maintaining venue records is a standard, singular interpretation in event systems.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details ... see the events happening there
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details and associated events is clear and not materially open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous association chain (sessions of attendees who work for sponsor? attendees linked to sponsor page? speakers vs. attendees).

evaluations.evidence: payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “registration process” refers to (camp vs. sponsorship vs. training) and what counts as “third step” if flows differ.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Assigning sponsors to content types is a clear action with a single main interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: The requested listing is clear and not materially open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged for an individual sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Charging a card for an individual sponsorship is a clear, standard payment requirement.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: “Link attendees” is ambiguous (manual association, self-claiming, bulk import, by company) and affects multiple possible implementations.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Updating one’s user profile is a common, singular interpretation even if fields are not enumerated.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup is a clear action with minimal interpretive variance.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet
evaluations.rationale: Tagging posts for Drupal Planet is specific enough to avoid materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is a clear capability with a standard interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading the blog is straightforward and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit that matches my brand
evaluations.rationale: “Matches my brand” is subjective and could drive different selection/filtering/approval behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Summit registration is a clear action with a single main interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: “Detailed directions” is vague (map link vs. step-by-step directions vs. transit/parking info), allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: The requested list is clear and not materially ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing registered attendees for a summit is a clear, singular requirement.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: “Basic information” is undefined and could include different fields (description, time, venue, speakers, capacity, etc.).

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing summit sponsors is clear and not materially open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: “Agenda” can mean multiple structures (sessions with times, topics only, speakers, breaks), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Remaining seat count is a concrete concept with a single main interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: “Specific details” is undefined and could refer to many different information sets and page elements.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: A list of summits is a clear deliverable with minimal interpretive variance.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Providing information about sponsorship levels is clear enough as an informational requirement.

evaluations.evidence: all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: “Long-form content” is an undefined category and could include different content types/fields, leading to materially different scope.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Adding a link from job listings to a sponsorship profile is a clear, singular interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous who/what “the sponsorship person” is (role, specific contact, form) and what “learn about” must include.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Posting a job is a standard action with a single main interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the job board is clear and not materially ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous distinction between “room” and “location” (room already implies location) and what a “time slot” refers to (session slot, training slot, summit slot).

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the schedule is a clear user goal with a standard interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: A final approved sessions list is a clear concept with minimal interpretive variance.

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Bulk-approving sessions as accepted is a clear administrative action.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Marking a session as accepted is a clear, singular operation.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “notification” means (email, onsite message) and what “evaluated” means (scored, accepted/rejected, completed review).

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous channel/content of “notification” (email vs. UI) and timing/trigger (on submit click vs. after validation).

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing one’s submitted session is a clear action with a standard interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp, so that I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether “register to speak” is separate from “submit a session” (speaker account/approval vs. just submission).

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session for evaluation is clear and not materially open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: “Personalize” is vague and could mean editing text, branding, layout, media, or widgets—materially different scopes.

evaluations.evidence: a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: “When they are” is ambiguous (start date only vs. start/end times, timezone, multi-day schedule).

evaluations.evidence: several choices of idividual sponsorship on the second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “several choices” means (how many/which tiers) and which “registration” flow/page numbering applies.

evaluations.evidence: easily find a link in the menu
evaluations.rationale: “Easily find” is subjective and can imply different UX requirements (placement, labeling, prominence).

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: Completing a user registration form to create an account is a clear, standard requirement.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: “Session information” is broad and undefined (title/abstract, time/location, speakers, track, materials), allowing materially different interpretations.
